Update System & Core Packages

Ensure the local package index is updated and all existing software is upgraded before adding new packages.

apt update && apt upgrade -y

Comprehensive installation list for productivity, media, and document management:

apt install -y sudo i3 xorg xterm brightnessctl pasystray mousepad feh thunar speedtest-cli pavucontrol flatpak libreoffice-writer libreoffice-calc libreoffice-impress libreoffice-draw mpv simplescreenrecorder xfce4-screenshooter ocrmypdf telegram-desktop lollypop gimp foliate qbittorrent persepolis dbus-user-session xdg-user-dirs xdg-desktop-portal xdg-desktop-portal-gtk fonts-noto-cjk fonts-wqy-zenhei fonts-wqy-microhei fonts-arphic-uming fonts-arphic-ukai firefox-esr engrampa pspp xfce4-power-manager papirus-icon-theme lxappearance gnome-disk-utility network-manager network-manager-gnome evince ristretto system-config-printer cups pipewire-audio-client-libraries libspa-0.2-bluetooth libspa-0.2-jack pipewire-pulse wireplumber pulseaudio libreoffice-gtk3 gnome-themes-extra adwaita-icon-theme adwaita-qt adwaita-qt6 qt5ct qgnomeplatform-qt5 dconf-cli libglib2.0-bin libreoffice-style-elementary -y

User Account & Sudo Configuration

Add your user account to the sudo group:

usermod -aG sudo ejmevardo

Passwordless Power Management

sudo visudo

Append the following line to the end of the file:

# Allow passwordless power commands for ejmevardo user
ejmevardo ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: /sbin/shutdown, /sbin/poweroff, /sbin/reboot

Flatpak & Flathub Support

sudo flatpak remote-add --if-not-exists flathub https://flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo

Reboot Session

sudo reboot

Initialization of Custom Scripts

Ensure scripts for session initialization and system dialogs are executable:

chmod +x ~/.xinitrc && chmod +x ~/.config/i3/scripts/lock_and_dim.sh && chmod +x ~/.config/i3/scripts/exit_dialog.sh

Mounting the Extended Data Partition

Locate the correct partition via sudo blkid, then create the mount point:

sudo mkdir -p /mnt/Extended
sudo chown ejmevardo:ejmevardo /mnt/Extended
sudo chmod 755 /mnt/Extended

Update /etc/fstab for permanent mounting:

LABEL=Extended /mnt/Extended ext4 defaults,errors=remount-ro,user,exec 0 2
sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo mount -a

Fix the NetworkManager applet issue

Remove existing internet connection configuration

sudo nano /etc/network/interfaces
auto lo
iface lo inet loopback

# Comment out everything below this line
# allow-hotplug wlp6s0
# iface wlp6s0 inet dhcp
#    Comment out existing lines, usually Wifi credentials

Edit network configuration file

sudo nano /etc/NetworkManager/NetworkManager.conf

Find the line from that file and change its value to true

[ifupdown]
managed=true

Combined Audio for Screen Recording

Load the `module-null-sink`

pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=Combined_Audio format=s16le channels=2 rate=48000 sink_properties=device.description="Combined_Audio_for_Recording"

Route your Microphone into the `null-sink`

First, identify the name of your microphone's PulseAudio source:

pactl list sources short

Look for an entry similar to `alsa_input.pci-0000_00_1b.0.analog-stereo` in the output. Then, route your microphone into the `Combined_Audio` sink:

pactl load-module module-loopback source=alsa_input.pci-0000_00_1b.0.analog-stereo sink=Combined_Audio

Configure SimpleScreenRecorder

  • Launch SimpleScreenRecorder.
  • Proceed through the setup wizard. When you get to the Audio Input page:
  • Audio backend: Select PulseAudio.
  • Source: From the dropdown menu, select `Monitor of Combined_Audio_for_Recording`.

Route System Audio to `Combined_Audio_for_Recording`

  • You need to tell the applications that are playing sound (like your web browser, video player, etc.) to send their audio to your new combined sink.
  • Start playing the audio/video you want to record (e.g., a YouTube video in Firefox).
  • Open `pavucontrol` (PulseAudio Volume Control) from your terminal or dmenu.
  • Go to the "Playback" tab.
  • You will see the application that's currently playing audio (e.g., "Firefox," "MPV," etc.). Next to its name, there will be a dropdown menu showing its current output device.
  • Click on this dropdown menu and select `Combined_Audio_for_Recording`.
    • Important: You'll need to do this for each application whose sound you want to capture during your recording session.

Adjust Volumes in `pavucontrol`

  • While recording, you might need to fine-tune the levels:
  • "Recording" Tab in `pavucontrol`: You'll see SimpleScreenRecorder listed. Adjust the overall recording volume here.
  • "Input Devices" Tab in `pavucontrol`: Adjust the volume slider for your `Built-in Audio Analog Stereo` (your microphone) to ensure your voice is captured at an appropriate level relative to the system audio.
  • "Playback" Tab in `pavucontrol`: Ensure the volume for the applications routed to `Combined_Audio_for_Recording` is at a good level.

Start and Test Your Recording

  • Go back to SimpleScreenRecorder.
  • Start your recording.
  • Play some system audio and speak into your microphone.
  • Stop the recording gracefully in SimpleScreenRecorder.
  • Play the recorded video file with MPV and verify that both your system audio and microphone audio are present and at acceptable levels.

Making the Setup Permanent Across Reboots (Recommended)

    sudo nano /etc/pulse/default.pa

    Add the following lines to the end of the file:

    ### For SimpleScreenRecorder - Combined Audio Input ###
load-module module-null-sink sink_name=Combined_Audio format=s16le channels=2 rate=48000 sink_properties=device.description="Combined_Audio_for_Recording"
load-module module-loopback source=alsa_input.pci-0000_00_1b.0.analog-stereo sink=Combined_Audio

    Save the file (Ctrl+O, Enter) and exit nano (Ctrl+X).

    Finally, reboot your system.

    sudo reboot

Fix Thunar "Open Terminal Here" (Custom Action)

If you encounter "permission denied" errors, add this custom action to Thunar:

1. Access Custom Actions:

Go to Edit > Configure Custom Actions...

2. Configure the Action:

Click (+) and fill in:

  • Name: Open New Terminal Here
  • Command: 
    sh -c "cd %f && exec xterm"
3. Set Appearance Conditions:

Under the "Appearance Conditions" tab, leave pattern as * and check Directory.

4. Save and Test:

Click OK. Right-click in any folder to test "Open New Terminal Here".
